title: Strength exercise to help make your bones stronger
claims: The Royal Osteoporosis Society recommends strength exercise on 2 to 3 days of the week, leaving at least a day's rest in between, for 20 to 30 minutes, working the legs, arms, back and stomach muscles.
It advises building up to 3 sets of each exercise, with 8 to 12 repetitions in each set.
It recommends doing one exercise from each of the hinge, push, pull and squat groups every strength session, plus a brace and either a lunge or step once or twice a week.
It advises using a weight that allows 8 repetitions with good technique; if 12 repetitions feel easy, use a heavier weight.
It advises talking to a doctor or physiotherapist before starting if you have had spinal fractures or many broken bones, or are recovering from a broken bone.
